claim.quote: A key result of this work is the measurement of the quantum evaporation channel's gain of 0.15 $\pm$ 0.01, which will enable $^4$He-based dark matter experiments in the near term.

key_value.note: Quantum-evaporation channel gain of HeRALD v0.1 (dimensionless).

name: First Demonstration of the HeRALD Superfluid Helium Detector Concept
notes: Listed on the TESSERACT papers page; published as Phys. Rev. D 110, 072006 (2024) (the arXiv abstract page gives no journal reference, so the publication year is not recorded).

summary.plain: A 10 g helium prototype showed for the first time that individual helium atoms knocked off the surface of the liquid can be detected, a signal the full detector needs. The prototype could already be sensitive to dark matter masses down to 220 MeV.
summary.technical: HeRALD v0.1 (~10 g): heat-free film blocking with an unoxidized Cs film, TES-calorimeter readout of scintillation and 4He quasiparticle (quantum evaporation) channels; quantum-evaporation gain 0.15 +- 0.01; energy threshold 145 eV at 5 sigma, corresponding to dark matter masses down to 220 MeV/c^2.

title: First Demonstration of the HeRALD Superfluid Helium Detector Concept
why_it_matters: The abstract says this gain will enable helium-4-based dark matter experiments in the near term.
